title: Publication Profile
description:
Validates files in core/reference/publication/. How a release reaches one portal: the submission method the portal supports, the console a deterministic browser run drives when it supports no API, what only a person can do there, and whether automated use of the console is permitted by the portal's terms.

DATA, not integration code: the publish step's adapters read it, and the pipeline never names a portal. Kept apart from core/reference/platforms/<id>.yaml on purpose - a platform profile is pinned by content hash by every game built against it and changes only with the portal's compliance rules; this changes with the portal's console and is pinned by a publication record, never by a game.

2.0.0 (docs/portal-publishing-architecture.md, Part 2.4) makes the console flow data: an ordered `flow` of named intents, each with a phase and a class (reversible | irreversible | human), the `session` and `identity` locators the executor reads before acting, the `status` words including the `pending_states` it never uploads over, the `fields` the console asks for, the portal's `content_policy` on generated text and assets, and the bounds of the agent's drift resolution (`adaptive`, `adaptive_bounds`, `dismissable`, `deny`). Breaking against 1.x: `verification` is now `status`, and `console.upload_max_mb` is now `constraints.upload_max_mb`. scripts/check-integrity.py adds what a schema cannot say: no cancel, withdraw or delete intent in a flow; every irreversible intent carries a profile ladder; every intent has a class.

Nothing here is a credential. Credentials are named (an environment variable the installation sets) and never written.

id.description: The platform id: core/reference/platforms/<id>.yaml must exist.

status.description: unverified: the console flow below has not been exercised against the live portal by a person; the publish step then stops HUMAN_REQUIRED before contacting it. A console profile goes verified only after a dry run reached save_draft and a person checked the draft.

sources.description: Since 2.0.0. The public pages the facts in this file were read from, and when.

prerequisites.description: What a person must have done or obtained before the portal will take this release, beyond the account and session `submission` describes: a written consent, a host or domain of their own, a declaration. Each is a person's act, never performed or assumed by the Factory. Readiness reads them (wgflib.publication.human_reason): an applicable prerequisite a person has not recorded in factory.publish.platforms.<id>.prerequisites_confirmed makes the platform HUMAN_REQUIRED with the prerequisite's reason. `when` limits one to a release whose game.config.yaml platform entry states those values (an omitted key is the profile default, which never matches); when readiness is not given the entry, every prerequisite applies.

reason.description: The human_required reason it stops with: legal (a contract, consent, account or commercial term), declaration (a statement a person makes).

when.description: Applies only when the platform entry has these values (game.config.yaml platforms[]).

note.description: What the person does or obtains.

source.description: The public page that states it.

unknowns.description: Since 2.0.0. What a person must log in to learn before this profile can go verified: every console fact the file does not state, named. A fact absent from the file and absent from this list is a defect of the profile.

method.description: The portal's supported way in, preferred in this order: an official API or CLI when the portal publishes one; the developer console by a browser run of this profile's flow when it does not; email or manual when neither exists. Never an undocumented API.

api.description: method api/cli only: the documented endpoint or tool, by name.

console.description: method console only: the console a browser run drives. Origins are the only ones the browser may reach; everything else is refused at the browser. (1.x carried upload_max_mb here; since 2.0.0 it is constraints.upload_max_mb.)

automation_terms.description: Whether the portal's terms allow automated use of its developer console, as a person established from the portal's own documents. unverified or prohibited: the publish step never drives the console and stops HUMAN_REQUIRED (reason terms-unconfirmed); an installation records a person's finding in factory.publish.platforms.<id>.terms_confirmed.

terms_checked.description: Who established automation_terms, when, from which document.

credential.description: The credential the adapter needs and where the installation keeps it - by variable NAME only. A storage state is a Playwright storageState JSON a person captured by logging in once; the step never types a password.

capture.description: How a person captures or rotates it.

human_required.description: What this portal makes a person do, whatever the method: login and its challenges, accepting terms, payout setup, a console switch the automation does not touch, the declarations (ownership, licensing, AI use, data collection) and the age rating.

content_policy.description: Since 2.0.0. What the portal says about generated content in the listing and the game, as a person established it. `unknown` is the honest default: a release whose listing copy is generated then stops for a person (human_required reason ai-text-policy) until the policy is recorded. `disclose` fills the portal's disclosure field only from a person's recorded statement.

source.description: The document the policy was read from.

adaptive.description: Since 2.0.0. Whether the agent may resolve drift on this portal's reversible intents (the bounded adaptive mode, docs/portal-publishing-architecture.md Part 2.6). It runs only when this says allowed AND the installation sets factory.publish.adaptive. Irreversible and human intents never adapt, whatever this says.

adaptive_bounds.description: Since 2.0.0. The drift-resolution budget. Configurable down from the design's ceiling, never up: at most 3 resolutions per intent and 10 per visit.

dismissable.description: Since 2.0.0. Accessible names of non-destructive overlays (cookie banner, tour popover) the agent may propose to dismiss when one blocks a reversible intent: "Close", "Got it", "Skip", "Not now", and their translations in the console's languages. A name here may not match the deny vocabulary (check-integrity.py).

deny.description: Since 2.0.0. Words the console uses, in its own languages, for actions no adaptive proposal may ever resolve to. Added to the base vocabulary every profile shares (scripts/wgflib/publication.py DENY_VOCABULARY: submit, publish, release, review, send, delete, remove, cancel, withdraw, archive, accept, agree, confirm, sign, pay, price, tax, rating, I own, licence, license) - typically their translations.

session.description: Since 2.0.0. How the executor tells, on the console url, whether the captured session is live and what stops it. Every challenge stops the step for a person (WAITING_FOR_HUMAN); no screenshot or snapshot is ever taken on a login, CAPTCHA, second-factor or anti-bot page.

identity.description: Since 2.0.0. How find_game looks for the game before anything is created, in the order of `portal_id_from`. A recorded id that resolves is used; any unrecorded match - a title match included - stops the step (duplicate-candidate). Creation happens only when every lookup ran and found nothing.

list_url.description: The console page that lists the account's games.

game_url.description: A game's page, with {id} for the portal game id.

row_id.description: Where a row carries the portal game id: an attribute of the row, or the text of a locator inside it.

title_match.description: Title comparison is exact after case folding; never fuzzy.

flow.description: Since 2.0.0. The console flow, ordered: named intents the executor runs deterministically, phase by phase. A phase with no intent here is a person's (HUMAN_REQUIRED with its list). A flow never holds a cancel, withdraw or delete intent (check-integrity.py): nothing the Factory runs may cancel a pending review or replace a build under review.

status.description: Since 2.0.0 (1.x: `verification`). How the portal's own state is read back: the words its console shows, and which of them mean what. Every word in a *_states list is one of `states`.

submitted_states.description: The portal holds the submission: under review or moderation.

approved_states.description: Moderation passed but the game is not live (Yandex's Verified with Postpone publication): neither submitted nor live.

pending_states.description: status_gate stops on these before any upload (review-pending): never upload over, replace or cancel a pending review.

constraints.description: Portal rules an adapter checks before acting. null: not documented (name it in `unknowns`).

postpone_publication.description: The portal can hold a verified draft unpublished; the adapter sets it so publication timing stays a person's.

max_new_game_requests.description: New-game moderation requests one account may have open.

resubmission_cooldown.description: The portal's documented wait after a rejection, as it states it.

fields.description: Since 2.0.0. What the console asks for, by listing field, with the limits listing-validation checks before G6. null: the console was not seen (name it in `unknowns`).

restrictions.description: Since 2.0.0. Known portal rules that bear on publication, each cited.

basis.description: Where a locator or fact comes from: observed on the live console by a person, documented on a public page, or a hypothesis nobody has checked.

locator.description: One rung of a locator ladder (docs/portal-publishing-architecture.md Part 2.7), in order of preference: role (with its accessible name), label, placeholder, text (exact), a stable attribute (testid), css, xpath (only with a recorded reason). Exactly one kind per rung. Never coordinates, never image matching; `index` only inside a container the ladder already pinned.

ladder.description: Locators for one element, tried in order; the executor uses the first that resolves to exactly one element and records which.

intent.description: One named step of the console flow: what the executor does, on which phase, and how much may adapt. reversible: may be resolved by the bounded adaptive mode on drift. irreversible: a profile locator only, live mode only, once, never adaptive; drift stops for a person (drift-irreversible). human: never automated - the step stops with the intent's note and url for a person to act in their own browser.

action.description: No check or tick action exists: a declaration checkbox is never ticked by the executor.

url.description: navigate: the url path (within allowed origins). human: where a person does it.

names.description: The accessible names, labels or placeholders an adaptive resolution of this intent may match, case-folded, in every language the console uses. An element named outside this list is refused, whatever the agent's argument.

value.description: fill, select, upload: a path into the shipped store listing, the release manifest, the package or the game identity - never free text. <locale> stands for each locale of a per_locale intent.

per_locale.description: Run once per locale the listing carries and the console asks for.

optional.description: The element may be absent (a field the console shows only sometimes); absence is recorded, not a drift.

expect.description: The post-condition checked after acting. A reversible intent whose post-condition fails may adapt once; an irreversible one stops.

max_count.description: Lists (tags, categories, screenshots): at most this many.

size.description: Images and video: the stated dimensions, duration or byte limit, as the portal states them.

listing.description: Where the value comes from in the shipped listing.

human.description: A person fills it (free text to moderators, a commercial choice).
